questions.question: Which of the following is a physical adaptation that can help an animal survive in a cold environment?
options: Being active only at night
Having thick fur for insulation
Migrating to warmer areas in winter
Hibernating in an underground burrow

questions.question: Which of the following is a behavioural adaptation that helps an animal avoid daytime predators?
options: Having camouflaged scales
Possessing sharp claws
Being nocturnal and active at night
Having a layer of blubber

questions.question: Why is maintaining a high level of biodiversity crucial for a habitat?
options: It ensures that only one dominant species survives.
It helps to maintain healthy, stable habitats.
It decreases the need for any producers in the food web.
It prevents any natural evolution from occurring.

questions.question: What is meant by the term "gene pool" in a species?
options: The total physical volume of water where a species breeds
The range of DNA and genetic variation within that species
The physical adaptations used to swim in aquatic environments
The artificial selection of organisms in captivity

questions.question: Why do ecologists use sampling to estimate the size of a population in a large field?
options: Because it is impossible to count every single individual in the entire area.
Because sampling guarantees that every organism is physically captured.
Because sampling is only done when there are no organisms present.
Because they want to change the genetic makeup of the population.

questions.question: What type of equipment is a quadrat, and what is it typically used to sample?
options: A long net used to catch fast-flying insects
A square frame used to sample plants or slow-moving animals
A sensor used to measure the temperature of soil
A glass trap used to collect nocturnal mammals

questions.question: Why is it important that quadrat sampling is usually carried out randomly?
options: To ensure that only the rarest species are counted
To avoid bias in the results
To make sure every single organism in the habitat is sampled
To select the areas with the highest number of plants deliberately

questions.question: Which scientific tool is designed specifically to help identify different species based on their characteristics?
options: A classification key
A quadrat frame
A pyramid of biomass
A gene bank

questions.question: Why are organisms in an ecosystem described as being interdependent?
options: Because they can survive completely on their own without other species.
Because they depend upon each other for the resources they need to survive.
Because they all belong to the exact same species.
Because they do not interact with their physical environment.

questions.question: What is the fundamental role of producers in a food chain?
options: They break down dead organisms to recycle minerals.
They make the food that all other organisms in the food chain depend upon.
They consume primary consumers to control their population.
They absorb organic matter from dead animals.

questions.question: Why do all living organisms depend on decomposers in an ecosystem?
options: Because they are the primary source of light energy.
Because they break down dead organisms and recycle useful substances for reuse.
Because they hunt and control the numbers of top predators.
Because they are the only organisms that can photosynthesise.

questions.question: How is biodiversity defined?
options: The total number of non-living components in an ecosystem
A measure of the range of living organisms
The speed at which energy flows through a food chain
The physical size of the largest organism in a habitat

questions.question: Which of the following is a physical adaptation of a plant designed to deter herbivores?
options: Growing its leaves towards a light source
Flowering only during the night
The presence of sharp spines
Shedding its leaves in the autumn

questions.question: What is an example of a behavioural adaptation in plants?
options: Developing a thick, waxy cuticle on leaves
Growing towards light sources
Having deep taproots to reach water
Producing sharp thorns on stems

questions.question: What do pyramids of biomass represent?
options: The total number of individual organisms at each stage in a food chain
The biomass of organisms at each stage in a food chain
The speed of reproduction of the organisms in a habitat
The amount of water contained within the non-living surroundings

questions.question: Where is the producer always located in a pyramid of biomass?
options: At the very top level
At the bottom level
In the middle level
It is excluded from the pyramid

questions.question: What data is used to construct a pyramid of number?
options: The total dry mass of all organisms at each level
The number of organisms at each trophic level in a food chain
The amount of energy lost as heat at each stage
The depth of the soil in which the plants grow
